name: SFTPGo
description: An SFTP server with a web admin and a web file client: virtual users with quotas and permissions, folders that can point at S3 or other storage, and event hooks. One container; user files and the SQLite database live on its volumes. SFTP itself is published on host port 2022, since a reverse proxy cannot carry it.

access.note: SFTPGo creates its administrator on the first start from the name typed here and the password generated here, so https://<domain>/web/admin opens on a login form for that pair; reveal the password from the Variables tab. The pair is read only while no administrator exists, so change the password inside SFTPGo afterwards. SFTP users are created from that admin page and connect to port 2022 on this host, which the firewall has to let through.

inputs.name: domain
inputs.label: Public domain
inputs.description: Optional; the address of the web admin and the web client. SFTPGo builds no absolute URLs, so nothing else here changes when it is set.

ports.name: http
ports.purpose: The web admin, the web client and the REST API

ports.name: sftp
ports.purpose: SFTP, which a reverse proxy cannot carry

volumes.name: data
volumes.purpose: Every user's files and SFTGo's own backups

volumes.name: state
volumes.purpose: The SQLite database of users, admins and folders, and the server's host keys

update.notes: SFTPGo migrates its database on start. The host keys are on the state volume, so clients see the same server identity after an update.

secrets.name: admin-password
secrets.label: Admin password
secrets.description: Only used to create the first administrator; change it inside SFTPGo afterwards.
